intro: Hi! Today you make your first real English sentences: I'm Budi. I'm from Bandung. This is my phone. It's new. In Indonesian we often say 'Saya Budi' with no extra word, but English always needs a small verb here: am or is. Warm-up: can you say your name in English?
teachingNotes: Core interference: Indonesian has no linking verb ('Saya guru', 'Ini tas saya'), so learners drop be. Always model the full sentence: I'm a teacher, This is my bag, She's a teacher.
Common errors to correct gently: 'She teacher.' → 'She's a teacher.'; 'I from Surabaya.' → 'I'm from Surabaya.'; 'This my bag.' → 'This is my bag.'

Forms in scope: I'm / I am, he's / she's / it's (he is / she is / it is) and This is. Accept short and full forms. Do NOT teach negatives or questions with be (only the fixed chunk 'What's this?'); they come in the A1 lesson 'The Verb To Be'.
Teach 'a' only as part of a chunk (I'm a student, It's a pen); the a/an rule comes in Basic Sentences. Avoid jobs that need 'an' (engineer, artist).
it's (= it is) vs its (= -nya, owner): point out the apostrophe. Use This is to show or name something, then It's to say more about the same thing.
A0 limits: no simple present beyond fixed chunks like 'I like…', no past tense. Keep sentences 2–5 words.

keyPoints.title: I'm … and I'm from …
keyPoints.explanation: Say your name or job with I'm (= I am). For your city or country, use I'm from …. Indonesian 'Saya Budi' has no verb, but English needs am.

keyPoints.title: This is … and It's …
keyPoints.explanation: Use This is to show or name something near you. Then use It's (= it is) to say more about the same thing.

examples.en: This is my phone. It's black.
This is my office. It's small.

keyPoints.title: Never drop be
keyPoints.explanation: Indonesian says 'Dia guru', but English needs am or is after the subject: She's a teacher. If a sentence has no am / is, add it.

guidedPractice.hint: You are talking about yourself, and you need the verb too.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete: ___ is my laptop. It's new.
guidedPractice.hint: You are showing something near you.

assessment.rubric: Correct: I'm Dewi / I am Dewi. 'My name is Dewi' is good English but not the target form = 70. 'I Dewi' = 0 (be missing).

assessment.prompt: Write in English: Saya dari Medan.
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'm from Medan / I am from Medan. 'I from Medan' = 0 (be missing). Missing 'from' = 30.

assessment.prompt: Write in English: Ini buku saya.
assessment.rubric: Correct: This is my book. 'This my book' = 0 (be missing). 'This is book my' = 30 (word order).

assessment.prompt: Complete the second sentence: This is my car. ___ red.
assessment.rubric: Correct: It's / It is. 'Its' (no apostrophe) = 50. 'It' alone = 0 (be missing).

assessment.prompt: Correct the sentence: My mother nurse.
assessment.rubric: Correct: My mother is a nurse. 'My mother is nurse' (no a) = 70. Any answer without is = 0.

assessment.prompt: Write in English: Dia (perempuan) dari Bali.
assessment.rubric: Correct: She's from Bali / She is from Bali. 'She from Bali' = 0 (be missing). 'He's from Bali' = 40 (wrong pronoun).

blocks.text: In Indonesian you can say *Saya Budi* with no verb. English needs **am**: **I am Budi**. When we speak, we join them: **I'm** (= I am). For your city or country, add **from**: **I'm from Bandung**.

id.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kamu bisa bilang *Saya Budi* tanpa kata kerja. Bahasa Inggris butuh **am**: **I am Budi**. Saat berbicara, keduanya digabung: **I'm** (= I am). Untuk kota atau negaramu, tambahkan **from**: **I'm from Bandung**.

rows.en: Hi, I'm Rina. I'm from Jakarta.
rows.id: Hai, saya Rina. Saya dari Jakarta.

blocks.text: Don't say *I from Surabaya*. Say **I'm from Surabaya**. The **'m** in I'm is the verb you need.

id.text: Jangan bilang *I from Surabaya*. Bilang **I'm from Surabaya**. **'m** dalam I'm adalah kata kerja yang kamu perlukan.

blocks.explain: I'm = I am. 'I' alone has no verb, and 'Me' can't start this sentence.

id.explain: I'm = I am. 'I' saja tidak punya kata kerja, dan 'Me' tidak bisa membuka kalimat ini.

material.title: Show things: This is … and It's …

blocks.text: *Ini HP saya* has no verb, but English needs **is**: **This is my phone.** Use **This is** to show or name something near you. Then use **It's** (= it is) to say more about the same thing: **It's black.**

id.text: *Ini HP saya* tidak punya kata kerja, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **is**: **This is my phone.** Pakai **This is** untuk menunjukkan atau menyebut sesuatu di dekatmu. Lalu pakai **It's** (= it is) untuk menjelaskan benda yang sama: **It's black.**

rows.en: This is my phone. It's black.
This is my office. It's small.

rows.note: What's this? is a fixed question
This is also introduces a person

blocks.text: **It's** with an apostrophe means **it is**. **its** without an apostrophe means '-nya' (owner). After *This is …*, the next sentence almost always needs **It's**.

id.text: **It's** dengan apostrof artinya **it is**. **its** tanpa apostrof artinya '-nya' (pemilik). Setelah *This is …*, kalimat berikutnya hampir selalu butuh **It's**.

blocks.explain: English needs is after This, and my goes before the noun: This is my house.

id.explain: Bahasa Inggris butuh is setelah This, dan my ada sebelum kata benda: This is my house.

id.title: Menunjukkan benda: This is … dan It's …

blocks.text: Indonesian often has no verb in these sentences: *Dia guru. Saya dari Surabaya. Ini tas saya.* English always needs a form of **be** after the subject: **I'm** (I am), **he's / she's / it's** (he is / she is / it is), **This is**.

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia sering tidak memakai kata kerja di kalimat seperti ini: *Dia guru. Saya dari Surabaya. Ini tas saya.* Bahasa Inggris selalu butuh bentuk **be** setelah subjek: **I'm** (I am), **he's / she's / it's** (he is / she is / it is), **This is**.

blocks.text: Check every sentence: subject + **be** + the rest. *Budi* + **is** + *a student*. If there is no am / is, add it.

id.text: Cek setiap kalimat: subjek + **be** + sisanya. *Budi* + **is** + *a student*. Kalau tidak ada am / is, tambahkan.

blocks.explain: After the subject (Andi) comes be (is), then the rest: Andi is my brother.

id.explain: Setelah subjek (Andi) datang be (is), lalu sisanya: Andi is my brother.

blocks.text: In a new class, a new office or a hostel you meet new people. With just **I'm**, **This is** and **It's** you can already say a lot. **Nice to meet you** is a polite fixed phrase for the first meeting.

id.text: Di kelas baru, kantor baru atau hostel kamu bertemu orang baru. Hanya dengan **I'm**, **This is** dan **It's** kamu sudah bisa bilang banyak hal. **Nice to meet you** adalah frasa sopan yang tetap untuk pertemuan pertama.

rows.en: Hi, Dimas. I'm Putri. I'm from Lombok.
rows.id: Hai, Dimas. Saya Putri. Saya dari Lombok.

rows.en: Nice to meet you. This is my friend, Eko.
rows.id: Senang bertemu denganmu. Ini teman saya, Eko.

blocks.text: Keep it short. Two sentences are enough for a first hello: **I'm Putri. I'm from Lombok.**

id.text: Buat singkat saja. Dua kalimat sudah cukup untuk sapaan pertama: **I'm Putri. I'm from Lombok.**

suggestedQuestions: What's the difference between it's and its?
When do I use This is and when It's?
Can I say 'My name is …' instead of 'I'm …'?

id.intro: Hai! Hari ini kamu membuat kalimat bahasa Inggris pertamamu yang sungguhan: I'm Budi. I'm from Bandung. This is my phone. It's new. Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita sering bilang 'Saya Budi' tanpa kata tambahan, tapi bahasa Inggris selalu butuh kata kerja kecil di sini: am atau is. Pemanasan: bisakah kamu menyebut namamu dalam bahasa Inggris?
